newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-BRAZIL ROUT BRINGS COPA TO LIFE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL ROUT BRINGS COPA TO LIFE.

text.p: Brazil routed Costa Rica 5-0 on Friday to bring the Copa America to life after the opening four games had produced only three goals between them.
Organisers will also have been hugely relieved that the 38,000 capacity Tahuichi stadium was nearly full for a double bill which began with Mexico beating Colombia 2-1.
Alarm bells were ringing after only 5,000 people watched Peru beat Uruguay 1-0 in Sucre on Thursday and just 10,000 saw the hosts beat Venezuela 1-0 in La Paz the same night.

But Friday's excitement, which almost inevitably starred Brazil's striking partnership of Romario and Ronaldo, cannot hide the fact that holding the Copa America in the middle of the region's World Cup qualifiers was probably a huge blunder.
The 12 teams have responded by bringing teams of varying strengths, ranging from full-strength to half-strength to virtual under-23 sides.
Brazil, who as world champions qualify automatically for France next year, and Costa Rica are two of the teams at full-strength.
For 20 minutes, Brazil struggled and the crowd at one stage chanted "Ole" as Costa Rica stroked the ball around.
Reality returned when midfield playmaker Djalminha scored direct from a free kick in the 23rd minute and Costa Rica captain Ronald Gonzalez put through his own goal 13 minutes later.
Brazil turned on the style in the second half with Ronaldo, who scored twice, and Romario each scoring superb individual efforts.
Later the hapless Gonzalez warned other teams: "We found that Brazil are more dangerous when they are annoyed. Brazil got annoyed when the crowd began whistling them early in the game."

Earlier, Luis Hernandez had scored twice in the first 15 minutes for Mexico but his niggly team were unable to create any further decent chances in the game between two of the teams who could be described as being at half-strength.

Colombia created numerous chances but their younger players showed the same failings as the more experienced ones as their poor final passes spoiled what was often neat approach work. A 60th minute goal from Hamilton Ricard was all they had to show for their pressure.

Brazil apart, Venezuela were probably the happiest team around after holding Bolivia to just one goal at altitude on Thursday. They had conceeded 13 in their previous two visits to La Paz, the capital.
Coach Eduardo Borrero said Friday: "This was not a negative result. We show that we have advanced."

Venezuela play Uruguay, who blamed the altitude for their shock defeat to Peru, in group B on Sunday in Sucre. Bolivia, meet Peru, one of the teams who are little more than an under-23 outfit, in La Paz the same day and will hope for more backing than they had against Venezuela.
